plot: On a windy sunset after the park walk Max is sure his favorite apple tree is sick because it drops all its leaves, and his honey plan only glues the leaves to himself; when he climbs up to say goodnight he finds tiny buds on every twig, Grandma explains the tree is only resting and keeps next spring's leaves safe inside, Bird spots her old nest in the bare branches, and the wiggling leaf pile turns out to be Nutty's warm winter bed, so Max gives the leaves back and wants to write to Luna, but he can't write.

beats.say: Grandma! Come quick! My tree is losing all its leaves!
Another one fell! And another! It's raining leaves!
My poor tree must be sick! I have to save it!
It's a windy sunset, the evening after the big park walk.
This apple tree is where Max naps, and climbs, and dreams.
All summer it was green and full. Now look at it!
It looks like a big brown broom. Upside down.
Bird, this is not funny. This is serious tree business.
Max, dear, look closely before you worry.
No time to look closely, Grandma! It's an emergency!
Funny. My old nest tree did this last year too.
Then we'll put the leaves back! Every single one!
All of them? Max, there are a million leaves!
Then I'll start with one. And then another one.
Max gathers leaves from the big pile by the fence.
The pile wiggles a little. Max doesn't notice.
Now I need glue. Something really sticky.
Grandma's honey jar! It's the stickiest thing in the house!
Max dips his paw into the honey. Sticky, sticky, sticky.
One leaf here. One leaf there. Hold on, little leaf!
But the leaves don't stick to the tree. They stick to Max!
Max! You're not a cat anymore! You're a walking leaf pile!
Get them off! They tickle my whiskers!
I can help! Can I lick the honey off? Please?
No, Dog! Well... okay, just one paw.
Mmm. Honey cat. My favorite flavor.
Then the wind blows harder. Whoosh! Ten more leaves fall.
It's getting worse! By morning, my tree will be bare!
Tonight is the first frost, Max. The rest will fall soon.
I tried my best. And I still can't save my tree.
Max sits under the tree, sticky, leafy, and sad.
Max, let's climb up and say goodnight. Like we always do.
Okay. But only because it might be the last time.
So Max climbs up, branch by branch, to his favorite spot.
Hello, tree. I'm sorry. I couldn't fix you.
Then Max sees something at the tip of a twig.
Wait. What's this? A tiny brown bump. And another one!
There's one on every twig! Hundreds of them!
Max looks at the next twig. And the next. Buds everywhere.
Are they spots? Is my tree getting spots now?
Now you're looking closely, Max. Good.
Those are buds. Inside each one is a tiny folded leaf.
A leaf? Inside? Already? But it's almost winter!
Your tree isn't sick. It's resting for the winter.
It lets old leaves go and keeps new ones safe in buds.
So it's not sick. It's sleeping! Like me after lunch!
And look what we can see now that the leaves are gone!
Up in the bare branches sits Bird's old summer nest.
My old nest! It was hiding behind the leaves all summer!
Bare trees have secrets. You just have to look.
But the fallen leaves are so sad. Nobody wants them.
Oh, someone wants them very much. Listen.
The big leaf pile wiggles again. Rustle, rustle, rustle.
Hey! Who's so noisy? I'm making my winter bed!
Nutty! You were in the leaf pile the whole time?
Of course! Leaves are the best blankets in the world!
Warm, soft and crunchy. And you kept taking them!
So that's why the pile kept wiggling!
Oops. Sorry, Nutty. I'll give them back. Not stick them back.
Fallen leaves keep little animals warm. And they feed the soil.
So in spring, your tree grows even stronger.
So the leaves didn't leave. They just got a new job!
Max puts every leaf back on Nutty's pile. None on the tree.
And I licked all the honey off. Teamwork!
Sometimes things that look like an ending are a getting-ready.
Max hugs the bare tree. Good night, tree. See you in spring.
I wish Luna could see this. She'd love the tiny buds.
Then why don't you write her a letter, Max?
A letter? Me? But Grandma... I can't write!
Can a cat who can't write send a letter?
